Based on the healthcare Q&A matches provided, it appears that routine placement of a nasogastric tube (NGT) in patients who have undergone laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (LSG) does not seem to be effective in reducing the incidence of leaks. The retrieved matches state that:

- Routine NGT placement in LSG patients does not reduce leakage rates.
- A study found no significant difference in mean %EBWL (extracted body weight loss) among patients divided according to resected stomach volume, but a greater resected stomach volume was associated with higher preoperative body mass index.

Therefore, it can be concluded that routine NGT placement in patients after LSG does not appear to be an effective strategy for preventing leaks.
